    22	direction is nonzero. This is a formalization-only consequence of
    23	`def:line-point-dist`, paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
    24	theorem aLinePointDist_zero_direction_mass (L : LdParams) :
    25	    avgOver (aLinePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    26	      if sample.1.direction = 0 then 1 else 0) = 0 := by

    28	  unfold aLinePointDist
    29	  rw [Distribution.avgOver_map]
    30	  have hdir (raw : LdSpace L) : (aLineDescOf L raw).direction ≠ 0 := by
    31	    intro hzero
    32	    have hcoord := congrFun hzero (chiIndex L raw.seed)
    33	    simp [aLineDescOf, LineDesc.direction, coordinateDirection] at hcoord
    34	  simp [avgOver, hdir]

    36	end

    13	The restriction is the proof-only conditioning used in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,

    23	/-- Probability retained by the proof-only first-line nondegeneracy
    24	restriction in the pasting argument for `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
    25	def nondegenerateLinePastingMass (L : LdParams) : ℝ :=
    26	  ∑ samples ∈
    27	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
    28	        (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
    29	    (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples
    30	
    31	/-- The retained product-law mass lies between one half and one. -/
    32	theorem nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds (L : LdParams) :
    33	    1 / 2 ≤ nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ∧
    34	      nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ≤ 1 := by
    35	  classical
    36	  let indicator := fun sample : LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) =>
    37	    if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0
    38	  have hmass : nondegenerateLinePastingMass L =
    39	      avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator := by
    40	    unfold nondegenerateLinePastingMass
    41	    rw [Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver, avgOver_prod]
    42	    change avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    43	      avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun _ => indicator sample)) = _
    44	    simp_rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (linePointDist_isProbability L)]
    45	  have haxis : avgOver (aLinePointDist L) indicator = 1 := by
    46	    have hindicator : indicator = fun sample =>
    47	        1 - if sample.1.direction = 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0 := by
    48	      funext sample
    49	      by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
    50	    rw [hindicator, avgOver_sub,
    51	      avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (aLinePointDist_isProbability L),
    52	      aLinePointDist_zero_direction_mass]

    54	  have hdiag : 0 ≤ avgOver (dLinePointDist L) indicator :=
    55	    avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun sample => by

    66	      avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun sample => by

    10	
    11	The conditioning supports the pasting argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,

    23	/-- The first-line nondegeneracy event has positive mass under the product
    24	line-point law. -/
    25	theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos (L : LdParams) :
    26	    0 < ∑ samples ∈
    27	        (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
    28	          (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
    29	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples := by
    30	  change 0 < nondegenerateLinePastingMass L
    31	  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) (nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds L).1
    32	
    33	/-- Proof-only question law obtained by conditioning the product line-point law
    34	on nonzero first-line direction and relabeling the two samples for pasting. -/
    35	def nondegenerateLinePastingDist (L : LdParams) :
    36	    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×
    37	      (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) ×
    38	        (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) :=
    39	  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))
    40	    (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0)
    41	    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map
    42	      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))
    43	
    44	/-- The proof-only nondegenerate pasting question law is normalized. -/
    45	theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    46	    (nondegenerateLinePastingDist L).IsProbability := by
    47	  exact (Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    48	    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map _
    49	
    50	end
    51	
    52	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    86	\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}
    87	
    88	Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
    89	The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
    90	$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
    91	$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
    92	players and every line pair, define a POVM by
    93	\[
    94	 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
    95	 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
    96	\]
    97	There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
    98	requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
    99	uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
   100	evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
   101	outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.
   102	
   103	The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
   104	joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
   105	defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
   106	$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
   107	the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
   108	answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
   109	distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
   110	family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
   111	\begin{align*}
   112	 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
   113	 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   114	 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   115	 &=4.
   116	\end{align*}
   117	The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
   118	is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
   119	the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
   120	polynomially small functions of $\eps$.
   121	
   122	For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
   123	\[
   124	 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   125	    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
   126	 \qquad
   127	 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   128	    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
   129	\]
   130	The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
   131	assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
   132	difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
   133	$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
   134	admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
   135	enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
   136	vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
